 UK Pump Prices Fall for a Second Week as Diesel Premium Widens
 UK Pump Prices UK pump prices fall for a second week as diesel premium widens Petrol drops 3.64p and diesel 1.42p Diesel premium over petrol reaches 29.70p Loading Stock video by African Creator via Pexels 
 Nov 17, 2026 
 UK Pump Prices Fall for a Second Week as Diesel Premium Widens
 UK road fuel prices declined in the week commencing 16 November 2026, according to the official GOV.UK weekly road fuel price statistics. The dataset, which tracks ultra low sulphur unleaded petrol and ultra low sulphur diesel alongside duty and VAT rates, shows both grades easing from the prior week while the gap between diesel and petrol widened. 
 Petrol averaged 167.07 pence per litre in the latest week, a fall of 3.64 pence from the 170.71 pence recorded in the week commencing 9 November 2026. Diesel averaged 196.77 pence per litre, down 1.42 pence from 198.19 pence a week earlier. The diesel premium over petrol stood at 29.70 pence per litre, compared with a retail transport fuel spread of 27.48 pence in the previous week.
 Fuel duty was unchanged at 52.95 pence per litre across the series, and VAT remained at 20 percent. The stability of the duty line means the recent movement in pump prices reflects other components of the retail price rather than fiscal changes.

 The latest readings extend a retreat from the highs reached in mid-October 2026, when petrol touched 175.28 pence per litre and diesel 200.04 pence per litre in the week commencing 12 October. Prices have eased over the subsequent four reporting weeks, with petrol down roughly 8 pence and diesel down about 3 pence from that peak.
 The longer series shows how far pump prices have travelled over the past year. In the week commencing 27 October 2025, petrol averaged 134.40 pence per litre and diesel 142.38 pence, with a retail transport fuel spread of 7.98 pence. Petrol moved within a narrow band through late 2025 and early 2026, bottoming at 131.46 pence in the week commencing 9 February 2026, before a sharp ascent began in March 2026.
 That climb was steep. Petrol rose from 132.14 pence in the week commencing 2 March 2026 to 158.17 pence by 13 April 2026, while diesel jumped from 142.15 pence to 192.14 pence over the same period. The retail transport fuel spread widened from 10.01 pence to 33.97 pence, its high for the series, before gradually narrowing through the summer and autumn.
 For transport logistics and commercial fleets, the recent softening offers limited relief given the elevated absolute level of diesel, the dominant fuel for heavier vehicles. Household mobility costs and retail forecourt activity are similarly shaped by prices that remain well above the levels seen a year earlier. The data does not identify the causes of the movements, and no single driver is attributed in the source.
 Duty and VAT treatment remained constant throughout the reported weeks, so changes in the headline pump price and in the petrol-diesel spread stem from the underlying product and retail components rather than tax adjustments. The weekly series is published as a CSV table covering pump prices, duty rates and VAT rates.
